Messages.Author: Petri Wessman
Messages.Body:
A couple of clarifications would be nice:

1) The Rulemonger pages have these entries (among others) for
Heidelburg Castle:

Heidelburg Castle may not be used during an action (including
during combat). [RTR 980707]

Heidelburg Castle may not be tapped "in response" to any
instant effect (because all effects in VtES are instantaneous
except for actions and certain combat effects). [LSJ]

I'm a bit unclear on what the net effect of this is. In particular,
can I tap the HC in response to someone's action (say I have a
Raven Spy on a tapped minion, and I want to move it to an untapped
one in order to block my predator's bleed)?

In other words, how is "during an action" defined?

2) Damage prevention cards can now be played any time during the
combat round. Does this mean that if some effect were to deal
damage "before range is determined" (for example), it would be
legal to prevent this damage at once and then move on to the "set
range" step?

//Petri

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Petri Wessman <or...@termiitti.akumiitti.fi> wrote:
> A couple of clarifications would be nice:
>
> 1) The Rulemonger pages have these entries (among others) for
> Heidelburg Castle:
>
> Heidelburg Castle may not be used during an action (including
> during combat). [RTR 980707]
>
> Heidelburg Castle may not be tapped "in response" to any
> instant effect (because all effects in VtES are instantaneous
> except for actions and certain combat effects). [LSJ]
>
> I'm a bit unclear on what the net effect of this is. In particular,
> can I tap the HC in response to someone's action (say I have a
> Raven Spy on a tapped minion, and I want to move it to an untapped
> one in order to block my predator's bleed)?

No. That is "during" that action.

> In other words, how is "during an action" defined?

Any time between the announcement of the action and the conclusion of
the action (inclusive).

> 2) Damage prevention cards can now be played any time during the
> combat round. Does this mean that if some effect were to deal
> damage "before range is determined" (for example), it would be
> legal to prevent this damage at once and then move on to the "set
> range" step?

Yes, provided the damage is preventable.

No.

> If not, why not?

For the same reason the acting minion can't skip the "before range"
part of combat and play a maneuver to keep his opponent from playing
Drawing Out the Beast.

Just because you get to go first doesn't mean you get to skip steps.
